title: Daily Routines
description: Master reflexive verbs to describe your daily schedule, learn time-telling expressions, and talk about habits and routines using frequency adverbs and sequence words.

grammar.title: Reflexive Verbs — Daily Routines
grammar.content:
Reflexive verbs describe actions you do TO YOURSELF. They use reflexive pronouns.

Reflexive pronouns:
- me (myself)
- te (yourself informal)
- se (himself/herself/yourself formal/themselves)
- nos (ourselves)
- os (yourselves plural, Spain)
- se (themselves)

Conjugation pattern for -AR reflexive verbs:
- despertarse (to wake up)
- yo ME despierto (I wake up)
- tú TE despiertas (you wake up)
- él/ella SE despierta (he/she wakes up)
- nosotros NOS despertamos (we wake up)
- vosotros OS despertáis (you wake up plural)
- ellos SE despiertan (they wake up)

Stem-changing reflexive verbs (A1 level):
- despertarse (e→ie): me despierto, te despiertas, se despierta
- levantarse (e→ie): me levanto, te levantas, se levanta
- vestirse (e→i): me visto, te vistes, se viste
- dormirse (o→ue): me duermo, te duermes, se duerme
- acostarse (o→ue): me acuesto, te acuestas, se acuesta

Common reflexive verbs for daily routines:
- despertarse (to wake up) — stem change e→ie
- levantarse (to get up) — stem change e→ie
- ducharse (to shower) — regular
- bañarse (to bathe) — regular
- lavarse (to wash) — regular
- cepillarse (to brush) — regular
- peinarse (to comb hair) — regular
- vestirse (to get dressed) — stem change e→i
- dormirse (to fall asleep) — stem change o→ue
- acostarse (to go to bed) — stem change o→ue
examples:
Me despierto a las siete. (I wake up at seven.)
Te levantas tarde. (You get up late.)
Se ducha por la mañana. (She showers in the morning.)
Nos despertamos temprano. (We wake up early.)
Se cepilla los dientes. (He/She brushes his/her teeth.)
Nos vestimos rápido. (We get dressed quickly.)

Me ducho todas las mañanas. (I shower every morning.)
Te peinas el pelo. (You comb your hair.)
Se viste con ropa elegante. (He/She gets dressed in elegant clothes.)
Nos bañamos por la noche. (We bathe at night.)
Se duermen a las diez. (They fall asleep at ten.)
Me acuesto a medianoche. (I go to bed at midnight.)

grammar.title: Telling Time in Spanish
grammar.content:
How to tell time:

- ¿Qué hora es? (What time is it?)
- Es la una. (It's one o'clock.) — singular!
- Son las dos. (It's two o'clock.) — plural for 2+
- Son las tres. (It's three o'clock.)
- Son las cuatro. (It's four o'clock.)

Half past:
- Es la una y media. (It's 1:30.)
- Son las dos y media. (It's 2:30.)

Quarter past:
- Es la una y cuarto. (It's 1:15.)
- Son las dos y cuarto. (It's 2:15.)

Quarter to:
- Son las dos menos cuarto. (It's 1:45.)
- Son las tres menos veinte. (It's 2:40.)

O'clock:
- Son las tres en punto. (It's exactly three o'clock.)

Minutes:
- Son las tres y diez. (It's 3:10.)
- Son las cinco y veinticinco. (It's 5:25.)
- Son las siete menos cinco. (It's 6:55.)

AM/PM:
- por la mañana = in the morning (until noon)
- por la tarde = in the afternoon (noon to ~8pm)
- por la noche = in the evening/night (~8pm to ~midnight)
- de noche = at night (~midnight to ~6am)

Example:
- Me despierto a las siete de la mañana. (I wake up at 7am.)
- Ceno a las nueve de la noche. (I have dinner at 9pm.)
examples:
¿Qué hora es? — Son las tres. (What time is it? — It's three.)
Es la una y media. (It's 1:30.)
Son las dos y cuarto. (It's 2:15.)
Son las cinco menos diez. (It's 4:50.)
Son las siete en punto. (It's exactly seven.)

Me despierto a las siete. (I wake up at seven.)
Salgo del trabajo a las cinco. (I leave work at five.)
Ceno a las nueve. (I have dinner at nine.)
Me duermo a las once. (I fall asleep at eleven.)
Me levanto a las seis. (I get up at six.)

grammar.title: Frequency Adverbs — Habits and Routines
grammar.content:
Adverbs of frequency tell HOW OFTEN you do something:

- siempre = always (100%)
- normalmente = normally (90%)
- generalmente = generally (80%)
- a veces = sometimes (50%)
- rara vez = rarely (10%)
- nunca = never (0%)

Position in sentence:
BEFORE the verb:
- Siempre desayuno café. (I always have coffee for breakfast.)
- Nunca como pescado. (I never eat fish.)
- A veces voy al cine. (I sometimes go to the cinema.)
- Normalmente trabajo en casa. (I normally work from home.)

Other frequency expressions:
- todos los días = every day
- los lunes = on Mondays
- los fines de semana = on weekends
- una vez al día = once a day
- dos veces por semana = twice a week
- tres veces al mes = three times a month

NOTE: 'nunca' can also go AFTER the verb with 'no':
- No como nunca pescado. (I never eat fish.)
But 'nunca' before the verb is more common: 'Nunca como pescado.'
examples:
Siempre desayuno café. (I always have coffee for breakfast.)
Nunca como pescado. (I never eat fish.)
A veces voy al cine. (I sometimes go to the cinema.)
Normalmente trabajo en casa. (I normally work from home.)
Todos los días camino al trabajo. (I walk to work every day.)
Los fines de semana duermo hasta tarde. (On weekends I sleep until late.)

Voy al gimnasio tres veces por semana. (I go to the gym three times a week.)
Ceno a las nueve de la noche. (I have dinner at nine at night.)
Me despierto temprano los días de trabajo. (I wake up early on workdays.)
Salgo con amigos los fines de semana. (I go out with friends on weekends.)
Nunca desayuno tarde. (I never have a late breakfast.)
Siempre leo antes de dormir. (I always read before sleeping.)

grammar.title: Time Sequence Words — Ordering Daily Activities
grammar.content:
Use sequence words to describe what you do in order during your day:

- primero = first
- luego / después = then / after
- después de = after (before a verb)
- antes de = before (before a verb)
- finalmente = finally

Grammar: after 'antes de' and 'después de', use the INFINITIVE form of the verb:
- Antes de DESPERTARSE, suena el despertador.
- Después de DESAYUNAR, voy al trabajo.

With a specific time, use 'a las' + time:
- Me levanto a las siete.
- Desayuno a las siete y media.
- Salgo a las ocho.
- Llego al trabajo a las nueve.

Common daily routine sequence:
1. Primero, me despierto. (First, I wake up.)
2. Luego, me levanto. (Then, I get up.)
3. Después, me ducho. (After, I shower.)
4. Después, desayuno. (After, I have breakfast.)
5. Finalmente, salgo. (Finally, I leave.)

NOTE: 'luego' and 'después' are often interchangeable, but 'luego' is more common in Spain while 'después' is used throughout the Spanish-speaking world.
examples:
Primero me levanto y luego me ducho. (First I get up and then I shower.)
Después del desayuno, voy a trabajar. (After breakfast, I go to work.)
Antes de dormir, leo un libro. (Before sleeping, I read a book.)
Finalmente, me acuesto a las once. (Finally, I go to bed at eleven.)

Por la mañana, primero tomo café. (In the morning, first I have coffee.)
Luego, preparo la mochila. (Then, I pack my bag.)
Después, camino al trabajo. (After, I walk to work.)
Antes de cenar, hago ejercicio. (Before dinner, I exercise.)
Finalmente, me duermo a las once. (Finally, I fall asleep at eleven.)

pronunciation.title: Reflexive Pronouns — Stress and Placement
pronunciation.content:
Reflexive pronouns are placed BEFORE conjugated verbs:

- ME despierto (I wake up)
- TE levantas (you get up)
- SE ducha (he/she showers)
- NOS despertamos (we wake up)
- OS vestís (you get dressed, Spain)
- SE duermen (they fall asleep)

When used with infinitives, they attach to the end:
- Me quiero despertar. (I want to wake up.)
- Quiero despertarme. (I want to wake up.) — SAME MEANING!

Pronunciation tips:
- me = meh
- te = teh
- se = seh
- nos = nohs
- os = ohs
- se = seh

NOTE: 'se' + 'me' = 'seme' (not 'se me') when attached:
- Se despierta (he wakes up)
- Se está despertando (he is waking up)
examples:
me = meh
- te = teh
se = seh
nos = nohs
os = ohs
se = seh

Me despierto a las siete. (I wake up at seven.)
Te levantas tarde. (You get up late.)
Se ducha por la mañana. (She showers in the morning.)
Nos despertamos temprano. (We wake up early.)
Se duermen a las diez. (They fall asleep at ten.)
Nos vestimos rápido. (We get dressed quickly.)

pronunciation.title: Time Expressions — Pronunciation
pronunciation.content:
Common time expressions:

- una = OO-nah (one)
- dos = DOHS (two)
- tres = TREHS (three)
- cuatro = KWAH-tro (four)
- cinco = SIN-koh (five)
- seis = SEHS (six)
- siete = SYEH-teh (seven)
- ocho = OH-choh (eight)
- nueve = NWEH-beh (nine)
- diez = DYEHS (ten)

Half:
- media = meh-DEE-ah (half)
- cuarto = KWAHr-toh (quarter)

Minutes:
- menos = MEN-os (less/to)
- en punto = en PUN-toh (exactly)

AM/PM:
- por la mañana = por lah mah-NYAH-nah (in the morning)
- por la tarde = por lah TAR-deh (in the afternoon)
- por la noche = por lah NO-cheh (in the evening)
- de noche = deh NO-cheh (at night)

Minutes 11-19:
- once = ON-seh
- doce = DOH-seh
- trece = TREH-seh
- catorce = kah-TOHR-seh
- quince = KEEN-keh
examples:
una = OO-nah
dos = DOHS
tres = TREHS
cuatro = KWAH-tro
cinco = SIN-koh
seis = SEHS
siete = SYEH-teh
ocho = OH-choh
nueve = NWEH-beh
diez = DYEHS
media = meh-DEE-ah
cuarto = KWAHr-toh
menos = MEN-os
en punto = en PUN-toh
por la mañana = por lah mah-NYAH-nah
por la tarde = por lah TAR-deh
por la noche = por lah NO-cheh
de noche = deh NO-cheh

Es la una y media. (It's 1:30.)
Son las dos y cuarto. (It's 2:15.)
Son las cinco menos diez. (It's 4:50.)
Son las siete en punto. (It's exactly seven.)
Es la una y veinticinco. (It's 1:25.)

pronunciation.title: Syllable Division — Rhythm of Routine Words
pronunciation.content:
Spanish syllable division helps with pronunciation:

- des-pER-tar-se (des-per-tar-se) — 4 syllables
- levan-TAR-se (le-van-tar-se) — 4 syllables
- du-CHAR-se (du-char-se) — 3 syllables
- ba-NAR-se (ba-nar-se) — 3 syllables
- des-a-YU-nar (de-sa-yu-nar) — 4 syllables
- al-MUER-zar (al-muer-zar) — 3 syllables

Syllable stress rules:
- Words ending in a vowel, 'n', or 's': stress second-to-last syllable
  - ma-ÑA-na (to-MOR-row) — stress on ÑA
  - a-MA-ri-llo (a-MAR-ee-yo) — stress on RI
- Words ending in a consonant (not n or s): stress last syllable
  - ho-BRAR (to work) — stress on BRAR
  - ciu-DAD (ci-ty) — stress on DAD

Accent marks:
- déspErTarse — the accent shows where the stress goes in the infinitive
- me desPIErto — no accent needed on stressed syllables
examples:
des-pertar-se: des-pER-tar-se (to wake up)
levantar-se: le-van-TAR-se (to get up)
ducharse: du-CHAR-se (to shower)
bañarse: ba-NAR-se (to bathe)
desayunar: de-sa-YU-nar (to have breakfast)
almorzar: al-MUER-zar (to have lunch)

mañana: ma-NYAH-nah (morning / tomorrow)
tarde: TAR-deh (afternoon / evening)
noche: NO-cheh (night)
ropa: ROH-pah (clothes)
zapatos: zah-PAH-tos (shoes)
libro: LEE-bro (book)

exercises.question: What does 'despertarse' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'Despertarse' = to wake up. 'Comer' = to eat. 'Dormir' = to sleep. 'Ducharse' = to shower.

exercises.question: How do you say 'I wake up' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Me despierto' = I wake up. 'Me duermo' = I fall asleep. 'Me levanto' = I get up. 'Me baño' = I bathe.

exercises.question: What does 'es la una' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'Es la una' = It's one o'clock (singular). 'Son las dos' = It's two o'clock (plural).

exercises.question: What does 'levantarse' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'Levantarse' = to get up. 'Ducharse' = to shower. 'Cepillarse los dientes' = to brush teeth. 'Peinarse' = to comb hair.

exercises.question: What does 'acostarse' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'Acostarse' = to go to bed. 'Lavarse' = to wash. 'Cocinar' = to cook. 'Leer' = to read.

exercises.question: How do you say 'every day' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Todos los días' = every day. 'Cada día' = each day (less common). 'Siempre' = always. 'A veces' = sometimes.

exercises.question: What word means 'first' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Primero' = first. 'Luego' = then. 'Después' = after. 'Finalmente' = finally.

exercises.question: Complete: '___ despierto a las siete.' (I wake up at seven.)
exercises.explanation: 'Me despierto' = I wake up. 'Me' is the reflexive pronoun for 'yo'.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Son las tres y ___. (It's 3:30.)'
exercises.explanation: 'Media' = half. 'Son las tres y media' = It's 3:30.

exercises.question: Complete: '___ como pescado. (I never eat fish.)'
exercises.explanation: 'Nunca' = never. 'Siempre' = always. 'A veces' = sometimes.

exercises.question: Complete: '___ las dos y cuarto.' (It's 2:15.)
exercises.explanation: 'Son las dos y cuarto' = It's 2:15. Use 'son las' for 2+ o'clock.

exercises.question: Complete: '___ me ducho, desayuno. (After I shower, I have breakfast.)'
exercises.explanation: 'Después' = after / afterwards. 'Después me ducho, desayuno' = After I shower, I have breakfast.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Primero me levanto, ___ me ducho. (First I get up, then I shower.)'
exercises.explanation: 'Luego' = then. 'Primero... luego...' = First... then...

exercises.question: Complete: 'Me acuesto a las once de la ___. (I go to bed at eleven at night.)'
exercises.explanation: 'Por la noche' = at night. 'Me acuesto a las once de la noche' = I go to bed at eleven at night.

exercises.question: Translate: 'I wake up at seven.'
exercises.explanation: 'Me' = reflexive pronoun for yo. 'Despierto' = conjugated form of despertarse. 'A las siete' = at seven o'clock.

exercises.question: Translate: 'I shower in the morning.'
exercises.explanation: 'Me ducho' = I shower. 'Por la mañana' = in the morning.

exercises.question: Translate: 'I have breakfast at 7:30.'
exercises.correct: Desayuno a las siete y media.
exercises.explanation: 'Desayuno' = I have breakfast. 'A las siete y media' = at 7:30 (seven and a half).

exercises.question: Translate: 'I never sleep late on weekdays.'
exercises.correct: Nunca duermo tarde los días de trabajo.
exercises.explanation: 'Nunca' = never. 'Duermo' = I sleep. 'Tarde' = late. 'Los días de trabajo' = on weekdays.

exercises.question: Translate: 'First I get up, then I take a shower.'
exercises.correct: Primero me levanto, luego me ducho.
exercises.explanation: 'Primero' = first. 'Me levanto' = I get up. 'Luego' = then. 'Me ducho' = I take a shower.

exercises.question: Translate: 'I go to bed at eleven at night.'
exercises.correct: Me acuesto a las once de la noche.
exercises.explanation: 'Me acuesto' = I go to bed (reflexive, stem change o→ue). 'A las once de la noche' = at eleven at night.
